## Color mode {#color-mode}

The Native and sRGB switch in the Display section. It works right away, without an apply step.

```text
A switch needs no root and downloads nothing. It makes two calls, as you.

1. GNOME's display service, the call Settings > Displays makes:
   D-Bus org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig, object /org/gnome/Mutter/DisplayConfig,
   method ApplyMonitorsConfig (persistent), for eDP-1 only:
     color-mode = 0 (default)     Native
     color-mode = 2 (sdr-native)  sRGB
   The layout, scale, resolution, refresh rate and every other screen are sent back exactly as they are.

2. colord, for color-managed apps. Only once 'ASUS color profiles' is ticked:
     colormgr device-add-profile <Built-in Screen> <profile>
     colormgr device-make-profile-default <Built-in Screen> <profile>
   Native uses the panel's factory profile, sRGB uses ASUS_sRGB.icm.

When the second call fails, the first one is put back.

The way back: pick the other mode, or press Undo in the message that shows for a few seconds after a switch.

The code is ColorController.switch and DisplayConfig.set_color_mode in quicksetup.py.
```

There is no checkbox to untick here: switching to the other mode is the way back.

## Color profiles

### ASUS color profiles {#display-color-profiles}

The panel's factory profile and the ASUS sRGB profile, on the built-in screen in colord, for color-managed apps

- **Guide:** [Display Color Profiles]({{< relref "/docs/hardware/color-profiles" >}})
- **Only on:** the Zephyrus G16 (GA605WV), the GNOME desktop
- **Marked:** Recommended
- **Source:** [the entry](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L3345-L3348) · [`on_color_profiles`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2781-L2804) · [`off_color_profiles`](https://github.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/blob/main/src/static/scripts/quicksetup.py#L2914-L2922)

**Turning it on**

```bash
# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Put the profiles in colord's own profile folder, where it reads them reliably
# prepared in your cache folder by this setup: the files published in the repository (the copy in this checkout,
# or else https://raw.githubusercontent.com/THectic-NL/Zephyrus-Linux/main/src/static/icc-profiles/), checked against the SHA-256 built into the setup, with the
# description rewritten to the name GNOME shows. Root installs them only while their SHA-256 still matches.
install -d -m 755 -o colord -g colord /var/lib/colord/icc
echo '1b1133904cd9afccfdaf7937f44b267b610fae877edf5e27c5fe0cf5615f7530  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
cmp -s /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm /var/lib/colord/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm || install -m 644 -o colord -g colord /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm /var/lib/colord/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm
echo 'a53e41ad5d19c7c49b385b428c74f06a8d321a7dc64a9fe7f447666629b524b9  /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm' | sha256sum -c --quiet -
cmp -s /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm /var/lib/colord/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm || install -m 644 -o colord -g colord /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm /var/lib/colord/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm

# --- As you ---

# Add the profiles to the Built-in Screen in colord
# quicksetup.py does this itself (register_color_profiles), with colord's own tool:
colormgr get-devices-by-kind display
# ^ the Built-in Screen is the display colord marks as embedded (eDP)
colormgr find-profile-by-filename /var/lib/colord/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm
# ^ colord reads a new file a moment after it lands, so this is retried for up to 10 seconds
colormgr find-profile-by-filename /var/lib/colord/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm
# ^ colord reads a new file a moment after it lands, so this is retried for up to 10 seconds
colormgr device-add-profile <Built-in Screen> <each of the profiles above>
# ^ unless the screen lists it already
colormgr device-make-profile-default <Built-in Screen> <the factory profile>
# ^ only when nothing but the automatic profile (the edid-*.icc colord makes itself) was in charge
```

- After switching GPU mode (Hybrid, Integrated, Ultimate), tick this again: each mode has its own display and its own profile.

**Turning it off (the way back)**

```bash
# --- As you, first ---

# Switch the screen back to its automatic profile and remove older copies
# quicksetup.py does this itself (release_color_profiles), and it amounts to:
colormgr device-make-profile-default <Built-in Screen> <the automatic profile>
# ^ only when one of these profiles is the active one right now. The automatic profile is the edid-*.icc colord made for the screen
rm -f /home/your-username/.local/share/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm /home/your-username/.local/share/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm /home/your-username/.local/share/icc/ASUS_DCIP3.icm /home/your-username/.local/share/icc/ASUS_DisplayP3.icm
# ^ copies an earlier version of this setup put in your home folder
rm -rf /home/your-username/.cache/zephyrus-setup/icc

# --- As root, one password prompt for all of it ---

# Remove the profiles from colord's own profile folder
rm -f -- /var/lib/colord/icc/GA605WV_1002_104D158E_CMDEF.icm /var/lib/colord/icc/ASUS_sRGB.icm

# --- As you ---

# Check that the screen kept its automatic profile
# quicksetup.py does this itself (restore_automatic_profile): when the screen is left with no profile at all,
colormgr device-add-profile <Built-in Screen> <the automatic profile>
colormgr device-make-profile-default <Built-in Screen> <the automatic profile>
```
